aoi.name: Tsho Rolpa, Rolwaling Valley, Dolakha, Nepal
aoi.source: 27 deg 52' N, 86 deg 28' E (= 27.867 N, 86.467 E), 4546 m a.s.l. -- Kayastha, R. B. and Maskey, S. (2024), "Glacial lake outburst flood (GLOF) modeling of Tsho Rolpa glacial lake, Nepal", Proc. IAHS 387, 59-63, doi:10.5194/piahs-387-59-2024. Concordant with Shrestha, B. B. and Nakagawa, H. (2014), "Assessment of potential outburst floods from the Tsho Rolpa glacial lake in Nepal", Natural Hazards 71(2), which gives 27.867 N / 86.467 E, surface area 1.537 km^2, max length 3.45 km, max width 0.5 km, elevation 4580 m.

valid_pixels.note: cloud, cloud shadow and defective pixels are invalid, not dry

snow_screen.citation: Hall et al. 1995; Hall et al. 2002

geometry_diagnostic.note: Diagnostic only -- the layover/shadow mask is NOT applied to the Phase 3 SAR mask; interpreting SAR water inside it is Phase 4's job (brief 7.3)

reference.dem_wbm_note: Copernicus GLO-30 water-body mask, epoch 2011-01-05 to 2014-09-08: an independent observation of the lake surface, not ground truth
reference.published_source: Shrestha, B. B. & Nakagawa, H. (2014), Natural Hazards 71(2) -- surface area 1.537 km^2; predates these 2023 scenes

findings: MNDWI is the same expression as NDSI (Hall et al. 1995), so it scores snow as water by construction. Index-only MNDWI over this AOI selects 32.2 km^2, 74% of it SCL snow/ice, merging the lake into a 13.3 km^2 glacier blob.

The MODIS water/snow discriminator (NIR < 0.11 reflectance) removes 85.5% of index-only water pixels and brings the largest body to 1.601 km^2 against a published 1.537 km^2, while still recovering 95.7% of the independent DEM-epoch water-body mask.

Single-scene Sentinel-1 amplitude thresholding does not work in this terrain: it selects 47.6% of the AOI as water, 42.3% of which lies inside the radar layover/shadow mask. Deriving the threshold from reliable pixels only does not fix it (-8.46 dB, still 37.5% of the AOI), so the problem is radiometric, not just geometric. This is an open design input to Phase 4.

A separation statistic computed by hard-splitting a sample at its threshold is inflated by truncation: a single Gaussian scores 2.67, clearing the >= 2 criterion. The two modes are therefore fitted by EM, which scores the same sample 0.99.

Under strong class imbalance the bimodality guard is not sufficient on its own: with 0.39% water, global Otsu still reports a separation but misplaces the threshold, selecting 43.5% of the image. Tiling fixes the placement.
